# PeTTa

> MeTTa (the AGI language of Hyperon) implemented in SWI-Prolog, with `petta` as
> its Python surface. Atoms are Python values, spaces are queryable stores,
> equations rewrite, and any Python library maps onto those forms. Every line
> below is signature, exact return shape, and the contract you cannot guess.

Install `pip install .` (runtime bundled) or point `PETTA_PATH` at a clone.
`from petta import MeTTa, S, V, val, expr, cast`. `m = MeTTa()` binds `&self`,
the same space the CLI uses.

## Atoms: built in Python, no engine call

`S.likes` -> symbol `likes`. `S["+"]`, `S["my-name"]` for non-identifiers.
`V.x` -> variable `$x`. `val(obj)`/`Gnd(obj)` -> grounded Python value.
Applying a symbol builds an expression: `S.likes(S.Ada, S.Music)` -> `(likes Ada Music)`.
`expr(S.f, 1, 2)` is the same as `S.f(1, 2)`. `parse("(f $x)")` -> `Atom`.
Kinds: `Sym`, `Var`, `Gnd`, `Expr`, all immutable, `__slots__`, `__match_args__`.
`Expr.head`, `.args`, `.children`; `alpha_eq`, `unify`, `is_ground`, `map_atoms`, `variables`.
Operators build terms, they do not compute: `V.age >= 18` -> `(>= $age 18)`;
`&` `|` `~` -> `and`/`or`/`not`; `+ - * / % **` and `@` build arithmetic terms.
There is no `//`: neither the operator nor an engine builtin exists.
Arithmetic on two grounded values stays ordinary Python. `Expr.__bool__` raises
on comparison and boolean heads, so `if V.x > 1:` is refused rather than truthy.
Equality is the one inversion: `a == b` is ordinary Python comparison answering
`True`/`False`, while `a.eq(b)`/`a.ne(b)` build the MeTTa terms `(== a b)` and
`(not (== a b))` for use in `where=` guards and equations.

## Running and querying: know the shape

`m.run(src) -> list[list[Atom]]`, one inner list per `!` directive.
  `m.run("(= (f) 1) !(f) !(+ 1 2)")` -> `[[Gnd(1)], [Gnd(3)]]`.
`m.eval(atom) -> list[Atom]` for a term already built in Python.
`m.value(atom) -> Any`, the single answer unwrapped, raises if not exactly one.
`m.query(*patterns, where=, limit=, timeout=, inferences=) -> Rows`.
  Variables shared across patterns join. `m.query(S.p(V.x,V.y), S.p(V.y,V.z))`.
  `where=` is a term the engine evaluates per match: `where=(V.n >= 60) & (V.n <= 70)`.
`Rows` is a list of `Row` with `.columns`; `row.x` and `row["x"]` both work.
  `rows.one()` (exactly one), `.first()`, `.column(name)` -> that column's atoms,
  `.table()` -> dict of columns, decoded to Python values,
  `.to_dicts()` -> plain row mappings, `.to_df()`/`.to_pl()` -> pandas/polars,
  `.build(column, cls)` rebuilds one column as that class, `_repr_html_` in notebooks.
`m.prepare(*patterns, where=) -> Prepared`; `.solve(given=...)` many times, `.columns`.
`m.stream(*patterns) -> Cursor`, engine-held, `.close()`, iterate lazily.
`m.assuming(*facts)` is a block where those facts exist and then do not.
Bounds on the evaluating calls: `timeout=` seconds and `inferences=` count on
`run`, `eval`, `value`, `query`, `stream` and `derivation`; `capture=` stdout on
`run` and `eval` only.
`m.parse`, `m.load(path)`, `m.save(path, format="metta"|"fast")` (atomic, fsynced),
`m.digest()` -> content hash of the space, store-independent.

## Spaces

`m.space(name)` selects, `m.fresh_space()` creates an unused one and is a context
manager whose exit drops it. A drop clears the whole life: atoms, equations,
subscriptions, import markers, tabling state. Named spaces compile into their own
module, so two spaces can define the same function. `(context-space)` names the
space the running code is in. `m.add(*atoms)`, `m.remove(atom)`, `m.atoms()`,
`m.count()`, `m.clear()`, `m.add_table(head, source)` reads polars/pandas/mappings/
iterables into `(head v1 .. vn)` facts. `&mork` and `&mork:name` are MORK-backed
when built; `&petta` is the library describing itself.

## Python functions as MeTTa functions

`@m.register_op` (alias `@m.op`) registers a callable; `m.unregister_op(name)` removes
every arity. Annotations become declarations in the engine's idiom: a `TypeVar` is
parametric, a `Union` declares one arrow per member, `Callable[[int],int]` ->
`(-> Number Number)`, `tuple[int,str]` -> elementwise. A generator is
nondeterministic, one answer per yield; returning `None` answers nothing.
Options: `name=`, `typed=`, `raw=`, `pass_atoms=`, `arities=`.
`@m.define` compiles the Python body itself into MeTTa equations; `.py` keeps the
plain function. Stacked clauses become first-match dispatchers. `m.fn(name)` calls
an engine function from Python; `m.type(cls)` registers a class with its methods.

## Types and cast

Types are optional atoms: `(: Ann Person)`, `(: age (-> Person Number))`.
A typed call silently answers empty for a mismatched or `%Undefined%` argument,
so `m.cast(value, type)` is the loud spelling: it returns the value or raises
`CastError` naming the types the value does admit. `Atom`, `%Undefined%` and `_`
are unchecked. `bool` spells `Bool` before `int` spells `Number`.
The target is positional-only. A concrete Python class target is also the static
return type of `cast`, `convert.build`, and `Rows.build`.
`m.arities(name)`, `m.is_function(name)` (global), `m.is_function_here` (space-local).

## Debugging

`m.trace(src, max_events=1_000_000) -> list[TraceEvent(depth, kind, term, answer)]`,
kinds `call` and `exit`; a reduction that fails leaves its call with no exit.
`m.derivation(atom, depth=None, timeout=, inferences=) -> list[Derivation]` with
`.rules`, `.facts`, `.complete`, `.truncations`; proof trees naming the equations
and stored facts behind an answer.
`m.why(pattern) -> str` explains one empty match in words. An empty result
returned directly by `m.query(...)` retains its query context, and
`rows.why()` identifies a pattern miss, failed join, or rejecting guard.
`m.lint() -> list[petta.lint.Finding]` reads stored program structure.
`m.stats()` is a with-block yielding `.inferences` (deterministic, gate on this),
`.cputime`, `.walltime`, gc counters, `.table_bytes`. `m.profile(src)` per predicate.
`m.prolog()` opens the SWI toplevel. Errors: `PettaError` base, then
`EngineError`, `MettaSyntaxError`, `CastError`, `CompileError`, `TimeLimitError`,
`InferenceLimitError`, `ResourceLimitError`, `Interrupted`.
`MettaOperationError(EngineError)` is a builtin refusing a value, with the parts
as data: `.operation` is what the source wrote (`+`, `min-atom`), `.kind` the
formal's functor, `.expected` and `.culprit` the type and offending value.
`m.eval_status(atom)` and `m.run_status(src)` pair each answer with the path
that produced it: `value` (an equation, builtin or special form applied),
`not-reducible` (no rule applied, the answer is the term itself), `empty` (the
branch pruned, answer `None`). A pruned branch and an unevaluated term are
different things that the answers alone cannot tell apart. `strict=True` on
`run` raises `StrictError` on a `not-reducible` directive, opt-in, since an
unreduced term is an ordinary MeTTa value.
Type checkers distinguish `SpaceName`, `MettaName`, and the closed
`SaveFormat` set. Their constructors are available directly from `petta`.

## Integrating any library

`petta.convert`: `project(obj)` -> `Projected`, whose `.atom` is the constructor
expression; `build(atom)` -> object, returning the atom unchanged when it cannot,
`register_type`, `unregister_type`, `declarations`. Dataclasses, enums, pydantic
and annotated classes all cross; enums project to symbols.
`petta.integrate`: `module_ops(space, module)` registers a whole module's callables,
`wrap_object`, `reflect`, paired register/unregister functions for protocol types,
formatters and reflectors, `SpaceProvider`, `Integration`, `discover` (entry-point
group `petta.integrations`). Installation is idempotent for a live space, and
`space.drop()` releases the installation record with that space's state.
`petta.foreign`: implement `Matcher`/`Enumerable`/`Adder`/`Remover`/`Clearer` and
`register_provider(runtime, name, provider)`, name starting with `&`, to make an
external store answer MeTTa matches; subclass `SpaceProvider` and answer `can_run`
per call, and an unsupported operation refuses loudly.
Conjunctive queries route per conjunct, so a foreign space joins with a native one.

## The rest of the surface

Eight of these load when first accessed rather than during `import petta`:
`aio`, `arrays`, `das`, `matching`, `measure`, `persistent`, `remote`, `testing`.
`dir(petta)` still lists each one. `subscribe` is eager, being part of the
write path.

`petta.arrays`: one operation vocabulary over any DLPack library (`install`,
`namespace_of`, `is_array`, `EmbeddingStore` with an exact faiss backend).
`petta.measure`: `install`, `ws`, `pairs`, `weighted_relation` for answers that
carry a score; `petta.matching`: `matcher`, `install_fuzzy`, `install_regex` for
matching that is a judgment rather than yes/no.
`petta.subscribe`: `m.subscribe(pattern, callback, on="add")` delivers inside the
write; without a callback events queue until `drain()`. `bridge` connects spaces.
`petta.persistent`: `PersistentFactSpace`, journalled, crash-recovering.
`petta.remote`: `serve(m, spaces=, token=, authorize=, ssl_context=)` and
`connect(url, token=, headers=)`; credentials require https, tokens compare in
constant time, only http/https schemes are accepted.
`petta.das`: SingularityNET Distributed Atomspace as a space.
`petta.aio`: `AsyncMeTTa` runs engine calls on one worker thread behind async.
`petta.testing`: the hypothesis strategies this suite fuzzes itself with
(`atoms`, `expressions`, `names`, `numbers`, `texts`, `symbols`, `variables`,
`grounded`, `numpy_scalars`) plus `benchmark_case`, `benchmark_counter_slope`,
and `measure_instructions` for deterministic benchmark gates.

## Contracts that cost real debugging

`match` evaluates its space and its body, never its pattern: patterns are
structural, so compute first and match after with `let`.
MeTTa equations are alternatives, not sequential clauses; a literal-headed default
needs a guard or it also fires.
A typed call rejects a bad argument by answering empty, not by raising: use `cast`.
Strings carry hyperon's five escapes (quote, backslash, `\n`, `\t`, `\r`); a raw
newline would split a MORK dump. A NUL byte is refused at the MORK boundary; the
native store carries it through save and load.
Symbols with whitespace, parentheses or quotes are refused at save, digest and the
MORK boundary rather than written unreadably.
An unreduced call is a non-empty answer, so test for truth with `any(a == True)`,
never "the result was non-empty".
Python `None` from an operation answers nothing, which is why an `Optional` return
declares the value type.
Engine calls belong to the thread that made the engine; `petta.aio` or
`remote.serve` own the crossing, `engine_thread` and `current_space()` report it.
Deterministic goal-call measurement is `stats().inferences`. Primitive work is
measured with `perf stat -e instructions:u`. Wall clock is advisory.
